definition: a large wild cat with a spotted coat that can run very fast

collocations.example: A sprinting cheetah can reach top speed in just a few seconds.
On safari we were lucky to spot a cheetah hunting.

definition: the leader of a clan or tribe

collocations.example: The tribal chieftain welcomed the travelers into his village.
After his father died, he became chieftain of the clan.

definition: a herb with long thin green leaves and a mild onion flavor

collocations.example: She sprinkled chopped chives over the baked potatoes.
Garnish the soup with chives just before serving it.

definition: a hard shiny metal used to coat other metals and prevent rust

collocations.example: The faucet has a bright chromium plating that resists rust.
Chromium oxide gives the paint its distinctive green color.

definition: slightly fat in a pleasant way

collocations.example: The baby had adorable chubby cheeks and a big smile.
He admitted he had grown a little chubby over the winter.

definition: to move slowly while making the dull repeated sound of an engine

collocations.example: The old train chugged along the quiet coastal track.
The bus chugged up the steep hill in low gear.

definition: a small piece of partly burned coal or wood that is no longer flaming

collocations.example: The toast was left too long and burned to a cinder.
Glowing cinders drifted up from the campfire into the night.

definition: careful to consider everything before acting or speaking

collocations.example: The company took a circumspect approach to the risky investment.
Officials remained circumspect about the details of the deal.

definition: a tank for storing water, especially for a toilet or building

collocations.example: They stored rainwater in a large water cistern behind the house.
The pump slowly fills the cistern again after each flush.

definition: a loud sharp sound made when one piece of metal hits another

collocations.example: We heard a metallic clank as the heavy gate swung shut.
The clank of chains echoed through the empty prison.

definition: an exciting ending that leaves you eager to know what happens next

collocations.example: The season finale ended on a dramatic cliffhanger.
The final vote was a real cliffhanger decided by one ballot.

definition: a small group of people who stick together and keep others out

collocations.example: The new student struggled to join the school's exclusive clique.
A few managers formed a clique that controlled every decision.

definition: a small mat placed under a glass to protect a table

collocations.example: Please use a coaster so the table doesn't get marked.
She bought a set of cork drink coasters for the party.

definition: a fine net of sticky threads made by a spider

collocations.example: He brushed away a cobweb that hung across the doorway.
Dusty cobwebs covered the corners of the old attic.

definition: a person or part that is a small but necessary part of a larger operation

collocations.example: Each worker is just a small cog in the machine.
The midfielder was a vital cog in the team's success.

definition: clear, logical, and convincing

collocations.example: She made a cogent argument for changing the old policy.
He gave cogent reasons for delaying the product launch.

definition: a high-quality brandy made in the Cognac region of France

collocations.example: He poured himself a glass of cognac after dinner.
They toasted the new deal with a fine cognac.

definition: relating to the colon and the rectum

collocations.example: Regular screening helps doctors detect colorectal cancer early.
She recovered quickly after her colorectal surgery last spring.

definition: a large stadium or amphitheater used for public events

collocations.example: The concert filled the downtown coliseum to capacity.
The wrestlers performed before a packed coliseum.

definition: comfortable and pleasant to use or wear

collocations.example: She curled up in a comfy chair with a good book.
After work he changed into comfy clothes and relaxed.

definition: matching something else in size, amount, or degree

collocations.example: The salary offered is commensurate with experience and skill.
Greater responsibility should bring a commensurate reward.

definition: a quality or feature that two or more things share

collocations.example: The partners discovered a commonality of interest in music.
Negotiators tried to find commonality between the two sides.

definition: an official announcement or statement, especially to the public

collocations.example: The two leaders issued a joint communique after the meeting.
The government issued a communique about the ongoing talks.

definition: a person from your own country

collocations.example: He thanked a fellow compatriot for the warm welcome abroad.
In the final she beat her compatriot in straight sets.

definition: an official who manages the finances of a company or government

collocations.example: The state comptroller reviewed the annual budget carefully.
The board voted to appoint a new comptroller this month.

definition: too much pride in yourself or your own abilities

collocations.example: The young actor was full of conceit after his first success.
She spoke about her talent calmly and without conceit.

definition: having the same center, with one shape inside another

collocations.example: He drew the target as a set of concentric circles.
The cut log showed many concentric rings.

definition: a state of agreement and peaceful relations between people or nations

collocations.example: The neighboring villages have long lived in concord.
The treaty was an important step toward national concord.

definition: a large open area in a station or airport where people walk

collocations.example: Passengers cross the concourse to reach the departure gates.
The crowded concourse echoed with announcements at rush hour.

definition: an apartment in a building where each unit is owned separately

collocations.example: They bought a luxury condominium overlooking the bay.
A new condominium complex is being built downtown.

definition: to combine two or more different things into one, often by mistake

collocations.example: Critics say the report conflates two very different issues.
People often conflate wealth with happiness.

definition: the place where two rivers flow together and join

collocations.example: The old city was built at the confluence of two rivers.
The streams form a confluence just below the valley.

definition: shaped like a cone, with a round base and a pointed top

collocations.example: She carefully measured the liquid into a conical flask.
The old tower has a tall conical roof.

definition: an idea or feeling that a word suggests beyond its basic meaning

collocations.example: The word 'home' usually has a warm, positive connotation.
For many people, that term carries a negative connotation.

definition: to spend time with someone, especially someone who is disapproved of

collocations.example: He was warned not to consort with criminals.
She openly consorted with the rival group at the party.

definition: a strange or complicated machine or device

collocations.example: He built a strange contraption out of old bicycle parts.
The kids rolled down the hill in a homemade contraption.

definition: feeling very sorry for something bad you have done

collocations.example: He offered a contrite apology for his rude remark.
She looked contrite after accidentally breaking the vase.

definition: a difficult problem or puzzling question with no easy answer

collocations.example: Managers face a conundrum over how to cut costs fairly.
The game presented players with a tricky conundrum.

definition: to rest and recover your health after an illness

collocations.example: She spent two weeks convalescing at home after surgery.
He went to the coast to convalesce after a long illness.

definition: curving outward like the outside surface of a ball

collocations.example: A convex lens makes nearby objects look larger.
The convex mirror gave the driver a much wider view.

definition: to have sex, especially said of animals

collocations.example: The male spider rarely survives after copulating with the female.
The frogs gather in spring, ready to copulate.

definition: a thick cotton cloth with raised parallel lines, used for clothes

collocations.example: He wore brown corduroy pants and a plain white shirt.
She bought a warm corduroy jacket for the fall.

definition: the dried seeds of the cilantro plant, used as a spice

collocations.example: Stir ground coriander into the stew for extra warmth.
The recipe calls for a teaspoon of coriander.

definition: a tight undergarment worn to shape the waist and body

collocations.example: She could barely breathe in the tight corset.
A maid helped her lace up the corset before the ball.

definition: something that forms a pleasing contrast to something else

collocations.example: The quiet garden was a perfect counterpoint to the busy city.
Her calm voice provided a counterpoint to his anger.

definition: to flow or move quickly, especially of a liquid

collocations.example: Tears coursed down her cheeks as she read the letter.
He felt the blood coursing through his veins.

definition: a person who attends a king or queen at court

collocations.example: The royal courtier bowed deeply before the queen.
The king relied on his most trusted courtier for advice.

definition: a lack of courage when facing danger or difficulty

collocations.example: Fleeing the scene was seen as an act of cowardice.
He openly accused his rivals of cowardice.

definition: clever at getting what you want, often by tricking others

collocations.example: They came up with a crafty plan to win the game.
It was a crafty move that caught everyone off guard.

definition: showing no intelligence or sensitivity; rude and thoughtless

collocations.example: He later apologized for his crass remark at dinner.
The festival was spoiled by crass commercialism.

definition: a gradual increase in loudness or intensity

collocations.example: The applause rose to a crescendo as she finished speaking.
A crescendo of noise filled the packed stadium.

definition: a small jumping insect that makes a chirping sound

collocations.example: The chirping crickets kept me awake all night long.
The children tried to catch crickets in the tall grass.

definition: the part of the body or a garment where the legs meet

collocations.example: There was a hole in the crotch of his old jeans.
The pants felt uncomfortably tight in the crotch.

definition: a container in which metals are heated to very high temperatures

collocations.example: The chemist heated the sample in a porcelain crucible.
Workers melt metal in a crucible before pouring it into molds.

definition: the soft white substance formed when milk turns sour, used to make cheese

collocations.example: The cheesemaker pressed the fresh curds into round molds.
The nursery rhyme describes a girl eating her curds and whey.

definition: a small dried grape used in cakes and other baking

collocations.example: Add a handful of dried currants to the cake dough.
She bought a warm currant bun from the bakery.

definition: knives, forks, and spoons used for eating

collocations.example: They received a silver set of cutlery as a wedding gift.
She laid out the cutlery before the guests arrived.

definition: a violent storm with strong winds rotating around a center

collocations.example: A tropical cyclone is expected to hit the coast tonight.
The cyclone struck the small island without warning.

definition: a tall evergreen tree with dark green leaves

collocations.example: A row of cypress trees lined the quiet country road.
The garden ended in a dark grove of cypress.

definition: a closed sac in the body that contains fluid

collocations.example: The doctor found an ovarian cyst during the scan.
She had a small operation to remove a cyst.

definition: a common wild plant with bright yellow flowers

collocations.example: A single dandelion flower grew in the crack of the pavement.
The child blew a dandelion and watched the seeds scatter.

definition: unpleasantly damp, cold, and often with a bad smell

collocations.example: The wine was stored in a cold, dank cellar.
The old tunnel was dark and dank.

definition: to mark a surface with patches of light and shadow or color

collocations.example: Sunlight filtered through the leaves to dapple the ground.
Soft shadows dapple the quiet forest path.

definition: a shortage or lack of something

collocations.example: There was a dearth of reliable information on the subject.
The team suffered from a dearth of young talent.

definition: to lower the quality or value of something

collocations.example: Printing too much money can debase the currency.
Cheap copies only debase the value of the original work.

definition: to cut off the head of a person or animal

collocations.example: The horror film shows a villain who threatens to decapitate his victims.
Rioters tried to decapitate the statue of the former ruler.

definition: to slow down; to reduce speed

collocations.example: The train began to decelerate gradually as it neared the station.
He decelerated the car before the sharp bend.

definition: a unit used to measure how loud a sound is

collocations.example: The decibel level at the concert was dangerously high.
Please turn the music down by a few decibels.

definition: to decorate something or someone, often for a special occasion

collocations.example: The hall was decked out in flowers and balloons.
The streets were decked with flags for the parade.

definition: to criticize something strongly and publicly

collocations.example: Campaigners decry the practice of testing products on animals.
The decision was widely decried as unfair.

definition: to cheat someone in order to get their money or property

collocations.example: He was jailed for trying to defraud investors of millions.
The pair were charged with conspiracy to defraud the company.

definition: no longer existing, working, or in use

collocations.example: The patent was owned by a now defunct company.
The once popular magazine is now defunct.

definition: a god or goddess

collocations.example: The temple was built to honor an ancient deity.
The people gathered to worship their chief deity.

definition: sad and disappointed

collocations.example: She felt dejected after failing the driving exam.
He walked away with a dejected look on his face.

definition: causing harm or damage

collocations.example: Smoking has a deleterious effect on your health.
Too much salt can be deleterious to health.

definition: a shop that sells prepared foods such as cooked meats and cheeses

collocations.example: She bought fresh ham from the local delicatessen.
We ordered sandwiches at the delicatessen counter.

definition: extremely excited and happy

collocations.example: The fans were delirious with joy after the win.
A delirious crowd cheered the returning team.

definition: the act of being rescued or set free from danger or harm

collocations.example: The old prayer asks for deliverance from evil.
The trapped miners prayed for deliverance.

definition: of very high quality and luxury

collocations.example: They upgraded to a deluxe room with an ocean view.
Fans rushed to buy the deluxe edition of the album.

definition: behaving in a wild and uncontrolled way

collocations.example: He suddenly broke into demented laughter at the joke.
She was almost demented with worry about her missing son.

definition: able to be shown or proved clearly

collocations.example: That the earth orbits the sun is a demonstrable fact.
The company has made demonstrable progress this year.

definition: quiet, modest, and shy in behavior or appearance

collocations.example: She gave a demure smile and looked away shyly.
A demure young woman sat quietly in the corner.

definition: a strong public statement criticizing someone or something

collocations.example: The speech was a public denunciation of corruption.
Leaders issued a joint denunciation of the violence.

definition: to make someone morally bad

collocations.example: Critics claimed the book would deprave the young.
They argued the film could deprave and corrupt viewers.

definition: to make someone unable to think or behave normally

collocations.example: Prolonged isolation can slowly derange the mind.
Grief had deranged him for a time.

definition: a word or phrase used to describe or identify something

collocations.example: The catalog adds a brief descriptor to each painting.
Scientists use a precise descriptor for every chemical compound.

definition: to treat a holy or respected place or thing with disrespect

collocations.example: Vandals were arrested for trying to desecrate a grave.
The ancient shrine had been desecrated overnight.

definition: deserving to be hated; very unpleasant or cruel

collocations.example: Attacking the elderly man was a despicable act.
The crowd booed his despicable behavior.

definition: waste material or debris left after something has broken down

collocations.example: Worms feed on the organic detritus in the soil.
The storm left a pile of detritus along the beach.

definition: a medical treatment that cleans the blood when the kidneys fail

collocations.example: She was on dialysis for years before her transplant.
He goes to the hospital for kidney dialysis each week.

definition: a piece of soft material worn by a baby to absorb waste

collocations.example: He quickly learned how to change a diaper.
Disposable diapers make up most of the market today.

definition: the movement of a group of people away from their homeland

collocations.example: Members of the Chinese diaspora gathered for the festival.
The diaspora community sends money home every month.

definition: a short statement that expresses a general truth or rule

collocations.example: She quoted the famous dictum that honesty is the best policy.
The company follows the dictum that the customer comes first.

definition: intended to teach something, especially a moral lesson

collocations.example: The novel's didactic tone annoyed some readers.
The play was written for a clear didactic purpose.

definition: to move away from the main subject when speaking or writing

collocations.example: The speaker kept digressing from the topic.
He tends to digress when telling a long story.

definition: a herb with feathery leaves used to flavor food, especially fish

collocations.example: She garnished the baked salmon with fresh dill.
He ordered a sandwich with a dill pickle on the side.
